title: ROUNDS: Source-Framed Diagnostic Revision after Multi-Turn Clinical Evidence
abstract: arXiv:2611.19636v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) achieve high scores on medical benchmarks, but does this performance translate into reliable diagnosis as a conversation unfolds? In diagnostic conversations, users can provide clinical findings across multiple turns, ask for a diagnosis without supplying answer options, and introduce opinions from others. Models must therefore form diagnoses from the available evidence and decide how to respond to subsequent advice. We introduce ROUNDS, a framework that evaluates these abilities after a fixed sequence of clinical evidence delivered over multiple turns. ROUNDS compares diagnosis with and without answer options, presents the same incorrect diagnosis under clinician and lay framing, and varies support for competing diagnoses in written five-clinician panels. translated_title: ROUNDS：多轮临床证据之后基于来源框架的诊断修正
translated_abstract: 大型语言模型（LLMs）在医学基准测试中获得了高分，但这种性能能否转化为随着对话展开的可靠诊断？在诊断对话中，用户可以跨多个轮次提供临床发现，可以在不提供答案选项的情况下要求诊断，并可能引入他人的意见。因此，模型必须根据现有证据形成诊断，并决定如何回应随后的建议。我们提出了ROUNDS，一个在经过固定序列的多轮临床证据之后评估这些能力的框架。ROUNDS比较有和没有答案选项时的诊断表现，以临床医生和外行两种不同表述框架呈现相同的不正确诊断，并在书面形式的五名临床医生会诊小组中改变对相互竞争诊断的支持程度。在来自五个数据集的七个模型、共1,035个病例上，有答案选项时的平均准确率为76.9%，而没有答案选项时仅为57.0%。临床医生框架下的误导性……（摘要原文在此处截断）
tldr: 本文提出ROUNDS框架，通过多轮临床证据后有/无答案选项的诊断对比、不同来源（临床医生vs外行）表述框架的误导诊断以及会诊小组意见变化，系统评估大语言模型在真实多轮诊断对话中形成与修正诊断的能力，发现无答案选项时模型准确率从76.9%显著降至57.0%。
en_tdlr: ROUNDS is a framework that evaluates how LLMs form and revise diagnoses after multi-turn clinical evidence under varied answer-option, source-framing, and panel-opinion conditions, revealing that diagnostic accuracy drops sharply from 76.9% with answer options to 57.0% without them.
